items.originalTitle: Toto Wolff on the moment Lewis Hamilton’s exit decided Antonelli’s future
items.summaryEn: Toto Wolff recounted the morning Lewis Hamilton left Mercedes and the immediate phone call that put Kimi Antonelli in the car.
detailZh: 沃尔夫谈汉密尔顿离队如何决定安东内利的未来
沃尔夫详述了汉密尔顿离开梅赛德斯的那天早上，以及随即的一通电话如何让安东内利坐进赛车
致梅赛德斯车迷。来自银箭车队的最新消息，包括F1新闻、车手动态、赛车研发以及来自Brackley和Brixworth的比赛分析。
接替七届世界冠军堪称现代赛车运动中最艰巨的任务。而对梅赛德斯来说，这个决定只用了几秒钟。
刘易斯·汉密尔顿令人震惊地转投法拉利，在F1围场引发轩然大波，但布拉克利车队的作战室早已着眼未来。在基米·安东内利于墨西哥城大奖赛历史性地锁定世界冠军后，车队领队托托·沃尔夫揭开了这位老将车手离开那个早晨的幕后细节。
“那天早上刘易斯来我家时，我当然知道发生了什么，”沃尔夫在赛后媒体职责中透露。“他确认要去法拉利的那一刻，我本能地知道基米要坐进那辆车了。”
“你到底在说什么？”
将一名青少年直接提拔进银箭厂队，被外界评论员普遍视为一场巨大赌博。然而，这位奥地利高管纯粹将其视为一次经过计算的风险，最坏的结果也不会从根本上摧毁车队。
他自己的高层领导团队则需要更多说服。早在安东内利在二级方程式（Formula 2）中真正站稳脚跟之前，这位亿万富翁联合所有者就已经在敲定接班计划了。
“我打电话给布拉德利·洛德（Bradley Lord）和詹姆斯·艾利森（James Allison），我说，‘基米（Kimi）要坐进赛车了’，他们问，‘你在说什么？’”沃尔夫（Wolff）笑道。
内部遥测数据提供了所有必要的依据。这位车队老板追踪了这位意大利天才在四级方程式（Formula 4）和区域方程式（Formula Regional）中的爆发式成功，认定按传统在青训方程式中历练纯属浪费时间。
“我们有数据，”这位梅赛德斯（梅赛德斯）负责人解释道。“不再需要任何确认了。他在四级方程式和区域方程式赛车中的成功已经证明了这一点。剩下的都很清楚。对我来说这从来都不像是一个风险。放手去干。提前进站（提前进站）。”
这种激进的提拔策略最终在2026年世界车手锦标赛上得到了回报。当被问及他究竟是在什么时候意识到这位新晋超级巨星注定要夺得冠军时，沃尔夫指出的是赛季中段一连串惊人的强势表现，而不是某一个决定性的弯角。
“我记性太差了，记不清是哪一场比赛让我觉得他能够做到。我觉得并没有某个特定的时刻，”他承认道。“只是当他能够一个比赛周末接一个比赛周末地……我想他连续赢了多少场比赛，四场？五场。五场。”
看着这位年轻挑战者接连打出那些统治性的比赛周末，让布拉克利维修区墙后的团队确信冠军已不可避免。
“最终我知道，如果我们能够为他提供赛车，他就一定会赢得冠军，”沃尔夫总结道。
detailEn: Toto Wolff on the moment Lewis Hamilton’s exit decided Antonelli’s future
Toto Wolff details the morning Lewis Hamilton quit Mercedes and the immediate phone call that put Kimi Antonelli in the car
For Mercedes fans. All the latest from the Silver Arrows, with F1 news, driver updates, car development and race analysis from Brackley and Brixworth.
Replacing a seven-time World Champion is arguably the most daunting task in modern motorsport. For Mercedes, the decision was made in a matter of seconds.

Lewis Hamilton’s shock defection to Ferrari sent shockwaves through the Formula 1 paddock, but the Brackley war room was already looking ahead. Following Kimi Antonelli's historic world championship clinch at the Mexico City Grand Prix, team principal Toto Wolff peeled back the curtain on the exact morning his veteran driver walked away.

"When Lewis came to my house that morning, I obviously knew what was happening," Wolff revealed during his post-race media duties. "The moment he confirmed that he was going to Ferrari, it was instinctively I knew that Kimi is going to go in the car."
"What are you even talking about?"

Promoting a teenager directly into a factory Silver Arrow was universally viewed as a massive gamble by outside pundits. The Austrian executive, however, viewed it purely as a calculated risk where the worst possible outcome would not fundamentally destroy the team.
His own senior leadership required a bit more convincing. Long before Antonelli had properly established himself in Formula 2, the billionaire co-owner was already locking in the succession plan.
"I called Bradley [Lord] and James Allison, and I said, 'Kimi’s in the car,' and they said, 'What are you even talking about?'" Wolff laughed.

Internal telemetry provided all the necessary justification. The team boss had tracked the Italian prodigy's explosive success through the Formula 4 and Formula Regional categories, deciding that traditional junior formula seasoning was a waste of time.

"We had the data," the Mercedes chief explained. "There was no confirmation needed anymore. He confirmed it by his success in cars in F4 and in Regional. The rest was just clear. It never seemed to be a risk for me. Go for it. Undercut."

That aggressive promotion strategy ultimately paid off with a 2026 World Drivers' Championship. Asked exactly when he realised his newly minted superstar was destined to take the crown, Wolff pointed to a staggering mid-season hot streak rather than a single defining corner.

"I’m so bad at remembering which race did I think he’s going to do it. I think there was no particular moment," he admitted. "It’s just when he was able to put race weekend after race weekend... I think how many consecutive races did he win, four? Five. Five."
Watching the young charger string together those dominant weekends convinced the Brackley pitwall the title was inevitable.
"Eventually I knew that if we are able to provide him with the car, that he’s going to win the championship," Wolff concluded.

items.originalTitle: How young can a Formula 1 world champion actually be?
detailZh: 一级方程式世界冠军的年龄可以有多小？
一名车手能否在17岁时成为一级方程式世界冠军？这听起来可能不可能，但在某些情况下，国际汽联的规定实际上允许这样做
基米·安东内利在2026年以20岁68天成为一级方程式世界冠军，打破了塞巴斯蒂安·维特尔之前保持的年龄记录，领先超过三年。但这就意味着安东内利是史上最年轻的一级方程式世界冠军吗？到目前为止是的，但总有人有机会来夺取这个意大利人的记录
那么一级方程式世界冠军的年龄可以有多小，安东内利失去年龄记录被更年轻的车手打破的可能性有多大？
部分答案可以在国际汽联运动规则附录L中找到。第13.1节（"完整超级驾照的资格"），第13.1.2条指出："车手必须在首次F1赛事开始时至少18岁。"
17岁驾驶F1：理论上可行
然而，这并不意味着只有18岁或以上的车手才能参加F1比赛。第13.1.2条还包含一个例外，该例外于2024年引入，内容如下：
"在国际汽联的单独决定下，如果一个车手被判定在单人座赛车比赛中最近和持续地展现出卓越的能力和成熟度，他可以在17岁时获得超级驾照。"
理论上，一个17岁的少年有可能成为一级方程式世界冠军，并且比安东内利的年龄记录提前两年多——前提是他们能在他们的第一个F1赛季中赢得冠军。
已经有过17岁的一级方程式车手：马克斯·维斯塔潘在2015年澳大利亚的首次亮相时年仅17岁零166天，使他成为一级方程式历史上最年轻的车手。
维斯塔潘在2014年就已经完成了他的第一个一级方程式测试，当时他16岁。同年，在他17岁生日不久后，他以周五练习车手的身份参加了他的第一个一级方程式周末赛。
弗朗茨·托斯特，托罗罗索车队负责人，马克斯·维斯塔潘，托罗罗索车队
但是，维斯塔潘令人惊讶的早期F1首秀产生了后果：国际汽联加强了超级驾照的要求，并将最低年龄从2016年起提高到18岁。年轻的车手还必须至少在单座赛车锦标赛中参赛两年，并积累40个超级驾照积分——维斯塔潘不会满足这些标准。
在引入年龄豁免后，安东内利（2024年）和阿维德·林德布拉德（2025年）都在17岁时获得了超级驾照。然而，当他们首次参加大奖赛时都已经超过了18岁——同样，2017年首次亮相的拉塞尔·斯特罗尔也是18岁148天，使他成为仅次于维斯塔潘的第二年轻的一级方程式车手。
从理论上讲，安东内利的年龄记录有可能会被打破。但要实现这一点，车手可能需要在他们的第一个或第二个赛季就成为世界冠军。这可能性有多大呢？
作为新手的赛车世界冠军：这曾经发生过吗？
F1历史记录中只有一位车手在首个世界锦标赛赛季就赢得了冠军——而且那是一个特殊情况：Giuseppe Farina在1950年赢得了首届世界车手锦标赛。
从那时起，最早赢得冠军的车手是在他们的第二个世界锦标赛赛季。这仅发生过四次：年、年、汉密尔顿（2008年）和安东内利（2026年）。
这四位车手中的三位在他们的新秀赛季已经非常接近冠军：Fangio在1950年只以三分之差输给了他的Alfa Romeo队友Farina；Villeneuve在1996年的冠军争夺战中输给了他的威廉姆斯队友Damon Hill，这是在最后的Grand Prix上；汉密尔顿在2007年获得了亚军，只比Kimi Raikkonen少了一分。
安东内利打破纪录并非不可能。
这些例子表明，这是可能的。但条件必须恰到好处——首先，一辆有竞争力的赛车，正如方吉奥（阿尔法·罗密欧）、维伦纽夫（威廉姆斯）、汉密尔顿（麦克拉伦）和安东内利（梅赛德斯）所拥有的。然而，很少有年轻车手一开始就能加入一支领先的F1车队，就像安东内利加入梅赛德斯车队那样。
因此，一个20岁以下的驾驶员成为F1世界冠军需要极其特殊的条件。但这样的情景确实可能发生。
detailEn: How young can a Formula 1 world champion actually be?
Could a driver become Formula 1 world champion at just 17 years old? It may sound impossible, but under certain circumstances, the FIA regulations actually allow it

Kimi Antonelli became Formula 1 world champion in 2026 at 20 years and 68 days old, breaking Sebastian Vettel's previous age record by more than three years. But does that make Antonelli the youngest Formula 1 world champion of all time? So far yes, but there is room for someone to come and usurp the Italian.
But how young can a Formula 1 world champion actually be, and what are the chances of Antonelli losing his age record to an even younger driver?

Part of the answer can be found in Appendix L of the FIA's International Sporting Code. Section 13.1 ("Qualifications for the full Super Licence"), Article 13.1.2, states: "The driver must be at least 18 years old at the start of the event of his first F1 competition."
Driving in Formula 1 at 17: Theoretically possible
However, that does not mean only drivers aged 18 or over are allowed to compete in Formula 1. Article 13.1.2 also includes an exception, introduced in 2024, which reads:

"At the sole discretion of the FIA, a driver judged to have recently and consistently demonstrated outstanding ability and maturity in single-seater formula car competition may be granted a Super Licence at the age of 17 years old."
In theory, then, a 17-year-old could become Formula 1 world champion and beat Antonelli's age record by more than two years – provided they managed to win the title in their very first F1 season.

There has already been a 17-year-old Formula 1 driver: Max Verstappen was just 17 years and 166 days old when he made his debut in Australia in 2015, making him the youngest driver in Formula 1 history.

Verstappen had already completed his first Formula 1 test runs in 2014 at the age of 16. Later that year, shortly after his 17th birthday, he made his first appearance at a Formula 1 race weekend as a Friday practice driver.
Franz Tost, Team Principal, Toro Rosso, and Max Verstappen, Toro Rosso

But Verstappen's remarkably early F1 debut had consequences: The FIA tightened its Super Licence requirements and raised the minimum age to 18 from 2016. Young drivers were also required to have competed in single-seater championships for at least two years and accumulated 40 Super Licence points - Verstappen would not have met those criteria.

Following the introduction of the age exemption, Antonelli (2024) and Arvid Lindblad (2025) both received their Super Licences at the age of 17. However, both were over 18 by the time they made their Grand Prix debuts – as was Lance Stroll, who debuted in 2017 at the age of 18 years and 148 days, making him the second-youngest Formula 1 driver after Verstappen.
In theory, Antonelli's age record could therefore be broken one day. But to achieve that, a driver would probably have to become world champion in their first or second season. How likely is that?
Winning the world championship as a rookie: Has it ever happened?
F1 history records only one driver who won the title in his very first world championship season – and that was a special case: Giuseppe Farina won the inaugural world drivers' championship in 1950.

Since then, the earliest any driver has won the title has been in their second world championship season. This has happened just four times: Juan Manuel Fangio (1951), Jacques Villeneuve (1997), Lewis Hamilton (2008) and Antonelli (2026).

Three of those four drivers had already come remarkably close in their rookie seasons: Fangio lost the 1950 championship to his Alfa Romeo team-mate Farina by just three points; Villeneuve lost the 1996 title to his Williams team-mate Damon Hill at the final Grand Prix and Hamilton finished runner-up in 2007, just one point behind Kimi Raikkonen.
Not impossible for Antonelli record to be broken

These examples show that it is not impossible. But the circumstances have to be right – above all, a competitive car, as Fangio (Alfa Romeo), Villeneuve (Williams), Hamilton (McLaren) and Antonelli (Mercedes) all had at their disposal. Very few young drivers, however, enter Formula 1 with a frontrunning team straight away, as Antonelli did with Mercedes.
It would therefore take an exceptional set of circumstances for a driver under 20 to become F1 world champion. But such a scenario could certainly happen.
keyPointsZh: 目前安东内利是史上最年轻的F1世界冠军，但未来可能有人打破这一记录。
keyPointsEn: Antonelli is currently the youngest F1 world champion, but there is room for someone to break this record in the future.

media.altZh: 维斯塔潘戏称与安东内利20岁时的最大区别：“他会说意大利语！” · 第 1 张

items.originalTitle: Max Verstappen jokes about key difference with Kimi Antonelli at 20: “He speaks Italian!”
detailZh: 马克斯·维斯塔潘开玩笑说，他与20岁的基米·安东内利的关键区别是：“他会说意大利语！”
马克斯·维斯塔潘以典型的风格回应了关于他与最年轻F1世界冠军之间最大区别的问题。更严肃地说，这位荷兰人欣赏基米·安东内利接地气的一面
马克斯·维斯塔潘，红牛车队，安德烈亚·基米·安东内利，梅赛德斯
在墨西哥大奖赛之后，基米·安东内利成为了F1历史上最年轻的世界冠军。这位意大利人打破了塞巴斯蒂安·维特尔保持的记录，维特尔在蒙扎已经表示，他很高兴看到安东内利打破这个记录，并认为记录是用来被打破的。
根据当前超级驾照规则，要想进一步降低安东内利的记录（20年、两个月和七天），将是一个巨大的挑战，因为有人必须在一个青少年时期就夺得首个世界冠军。
所有这些都凸显了安东内利成就的特殊性，尽管在意大利人获得冠军之前，维斯塔潘给出了一个相当平淡的回答，当被问及究竟是什么让这位梅赛德斯车手与大多数年轻车手不同时：“更多的天赋。”
当被问及这究竟是否如此简单时，这位四次世界冠军继续说道：“嗯，这当然有很大帮助。当然，他从小就有父亲的正确指导。他的父亲对赛车了解得比普通父亲多得多，如果你的儿子又有巨大的天赋，这已经帮了很大忙。”
在马克罗·安东内利的指导下，自然也有梅赛德斯的支持和信任，这是安东内利本人经常强调的。车队负责人托托·沃尔夫始终支持他的车手，甚至在去年困难的时候也是如此，而且有经验丰富的彼得·邦宁顿等人在他身边工作，安东内利几乎不可能希望有一个更好的环境。
当被问及安东内利拥有什么特质是20岁的维斯塔潘自己没有的时，荷兰人带着一脸严肃地笑了起来：“嗯，他会说意大利语……”
刘易斯·汉密尔顿、法拉利、维斯塔潘、红牛车队、安德烈亚·基米·安东内利、梅赛德斯
除了维斯塔潘的意大利语词汇量远不如安东内利之外，这位红牛车手强调这两个情况根本无法比较。
“你不能比较。我17岁就开始参加一级方程式赛车，很长一段时间里我都没有驾驶过能够为我争夺冠军的赛车，”维斯塔潘说。“这显然是最大的问题，但基米在那个年龄就能取得如此好的成绩非常令人印象深刻。”
凭借这些话，维斯塔潘自然是在提及他在托罗罗索的起步以及他在红牛的前几年，那段时间尤其困难，因为雷诺引擎表现不佳。因此，维斯塔潘只能争取个人分站胜利，直到2021年，也就是他的第七个F1赛季，他才有机会挑战车手总冠军。
由于缺乏有竞争力的赛车，前几年的表现自然让人感到沮丧，但这也给了这位荷兰人一个相对远离聚光灯的机会来发展。根据维斯塔潘的说法，安东内利没有这样的机会，因为他直接加入了一支顶级车队。
“我认为去年在某些时刻对他来说很困难。但当然，你也会从中学到东西，这些事情也是成长的一部分。在一个新手的赛季中，这是正常的，”维斯塔潘说。
“当你为顶级车队效力时，一切都会受到更严格的审查。你无法真正远离聚光灯来发展，但他很好地处理了这一点，为今年做好了准备。他从本赛季一开始就表现得很好。”
除了安东内利作为一名车手的品质，维斯塔潘还认为另一个方面甚至更重要：这位20岁的意大利人作为一个人是如何表现自己的，以及他似乎不受名气的干扰。安东内利很接地气，维斯塔潘表示这正是他最欣赏的：“他只是一个普通人。他不会表现得像摇滚明星或超级巨星。他非常真诚。他有一颗善良的心，我真的很欣赏这一点。
detailEn: Max Verstappen jokes about key difference with Kimi Antonelli at 20: “He speaks Italian!”

Max Verstappen responds in typical fashion when asked about the biggest difference between himself and the youngest F1 world champion. On a more serious note, the Dutchman appreciates how down-to-earth Kimi Antonelli is
Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes

Following the Mexico Grand Prix, Kimi Antonelli has entered the history books as Formula 1’s youngest-ever world champion. The Italian has taken the record from Sebastian Vettel, who had already said at Monza that he would be delighted for Antonelli to break it and that records are there to be broken.

Under the current superlicence rules, it will be an enormous challenge to lower Antonelli's record (20 years, two months and seven days) any further, as someone would have to clinch a maiden world title while a teenager.

All of this underlines just how special Antonelli's achievement is, although Verstappen gave a rather matter-of-fact response shortly before the Italian secured the title when asked what exactly sets the Mercedes protege apart from most young drivers: “More talent.”

Asked whether it really is that simple, the four-time world champion continued: “Well, that certainly helps a lot. And of course, he's also had proper guidance from a very young age with his father. His dad knows a lot more about racing than the average father, and if your son then has a huge amount of talent, that already helps a lot.”

Alongside Marco Antonelli's guidance, there is naturally also the trust and support of Mercedes, something Antonelli himself regularly highlights. Team principal Toto Wolff has always stood by his protege, even during the difficult moments last year, and with the experienced Peter Bonnington among those working alongside him, Antonelli could hardly wish for a better environment.

When Verstappen is asked what quality Antonelli possesses that Verstappen himself did not have at the age of 20, the Dutchman raises a laugh by responding with a completely straight face: “Well, he speaks Italian…”
Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari, Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes
Aside from the fact that Verstappen's Italian vocabulary is significantly less impressive, the Red Bull driver stresses that the two situations cannot really be compared.

“You can't compare it. I started in Formula 1 when I was 17, and for a very long time I wasn't driving a car with which I could fight for the championship,” Verstappen said. “That was obviously the biggest problem, but the fact that Kimi is doing so well at that age is very impressive.”

With those words, Verstappen is naturally referring to his start at Toro Rosso and his first years at Red Bull, which were particularly difficult because of the underperforming Renault engine. As a result, Verstappen could only fight for individual race wins and did not have the machinery to challenge for the title for the first time until 2021, his seventh F1 season.

Although the preceding years were understandably frustrating because of the lack of competitive machinery, they did give the Dutchman the opportunity to develop relatively away from the spotlight. According to Verstappen, Antonelli did not have that opportunity because he stepped straight into a top team.

“I think last year was difficult for him at certain moments. But of course, you learn from that as well, and those things also need to happen to grow. That's normal in a rookie season,” Verstappen said.

“When you drive for a top team, everything gets scrutinised more closely. You can't really develop away from the spotlight, but he handled that very well heading into this year. He was right there from the very beginning of this season.”

Aside from Antonelli's qualities as a driver, Verstappen considers one other aspect even more important: how the 20-year-old Italian conducts himself as a person and how he is seemingly unaffected by fame. Antonelli is down-to-earth, and Verstappen says that is what he appreciates most: “He's just a normal guy. He doesn't act like he's a rock star or a superstar. He's just very genuine. He has a good heart, and I really appreciate that.”
keyPointsZh: 维特尔表示很高兴看到安东内利打破记录。
keyPointsEn: Vettel expressed his delight at Antonelli breaking the record.
